```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 500000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1: Manual scaling of age

```{r task1-zscore}
age_z <- (health_data$age - mean(health_data$age, na.rm = TRUE)) /
           sd(health_data$age, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Mean of age_z:", round(mean(age_z, na.rm = TRUE), 6), "\n")
cat("SD of age_z:  ", round(sd(age_z, na.rm = TRUE), 6), "\n")
# Mean ≈ 0 (within floating-point precision), SD = 1 exactly.
```

```{r task1-minmax}
age_mm <- (health_data$age - min(health_data$age, na.rm = TRUE)) /
           (max(health_data$age, na.rm = TRUE) - min(health_data$age, na.rm = TRUE))

cat("Min of age_mm:", round(min(age_mm, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
cat("Max of age_mm:", round(max(age_mm, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
# Min = 0.0, Max = 1.0
```

## Task 2: Dummy encoding for plan_tier

```{r task2-dummy-recipe}
rec_dummy <- recipe(churned ~ plan_tier, data = health_data) |>
  step_dummy(plan_tier)

rec_dummy_prepped <- prep(rec_dummy, training = health_data)
dummy_result      <- bake(rec_dummy_prepped, new_data = health_data)

names(dummy_result)
# Output: "churned", "plan_tier_Gold", "plan_tier_Platinum", "plan_tier_Silver"
# "Bronze" is the reference level (alphabetically first → dropped by default).
# 3 dummy columns for 4 categories — as expected (k - 1 = 3).
```

## Task 3: Full preprocessing pipeline

```{r task3-split}
set.seed(602)
split <- initial_split(health_data, prop = 0.80, strata = churned)
train <- training(split)
test  <- testing(split)
cat("Train:", nrow(train), " | Test:", nrow(test), "\n")
```

```{r task3-recipe}
rec_full <- recipe(
  churned ~ age + bmi + income + plan_tier + education + num_claims + num_chronic_conditions,
  data = train
) |>
  step_impute_median(income, bmi) |>
  step_impute_mode(plan_tier, education) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
```

```{r task3-prep-bake}
rec_full_prepped <- prep(rec_full, training = train)
train_baked      <- bake(rec_full_prepped, new_data = train)
test_baked       <- bake(rec_full_prepped, new_data = test)

glimpse(train_baked)
```

## Task 4: Verify the baked dataset

```{r task4-check-missing}
total_missing <- sum(is.na(train_baked))
cat("Missing values in baked training set:", total_missing, "\n")
# Should be 0
```

```{r task4-check-scale}
train_baked |>
  summarise(
    age_mean    = round(mean(age), 4),
    age_sd      = round(sd(age), 4),
    income_mean = round(mean(income), 4),
    income_sd   = round(sd(income), 4)
  )
# age_mean ≈ 0, age_sd ≈ 1; income_mean ≈ 0, income_sd ≈ 1
```

```{r task4-check-dummies}
names(train_baked)[grepl("plan_tier", names(train_baked))]
# plan_tier_Gold, plan_tier_Platinum, plan_tier_Silver
# Reference level: Bronze (dropped)
```

## Task 5: PCA for dimensionality reduction

```{r task5-setup}
library(broom)

set.seed(602)
health_small <- simulate_bdat602(n = 10000, seed = 602)

pca_vars <- c("age", "bmi", "income", "premium", "deductible",
              "num_chronic_conditions", "num_visits",
              "num_prescriptions", "num_hospital_admissions",
              "num_claims", "avg_past_claim", "claim_amount",
              "app_logins_monthly", "support_calls", "policy_age_months")
```

```{r task5-recipe}
pca_rec <- recipe(~ ., data = health_small[, pca_vars]) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_pca(all_numeric_predictors(), num_comp = 5)

pca_prep   <- prep(pca_rec)
pca_scores <- bake(pca_prep, new_data = NULL)

head(pca_scores)
# Columns PC1 through PC5; each row is the projection of one policyholder
# onto the five principal component axes.
```

```{r task5-scree}
tidy(pca_prep, number = 2, type = "variance") |>
  filter(terms == "percent variance") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = component, y = value)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(group = 1, colour = "red") +
  labs(title = "Scree Plot: Variance Explained by Each PC",
       x = "Principal Component", y = "% Variance Explained") +
  theme_minimal()

# Cumulative variance — how many components reach 60%?
tidy(pca_prep, number = 2, type = "variance") |>
  filter(terms == "cumulative percent variance") |>
  filter(value >= 60) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)
# Typically 3–4 components reach 60% for this dataset.
# Each component independently explains less and less: PC1 ~20%, PC2 ~14%, etc.
```

```{r task5-loadings}
pc1_loadings <- tidy(pca_prep, number = 2, type = "coef") |>
  filter(component == "PC1") |>
  mutate(abs_loading = abs(value)) |>
  arrange(desc(abs_loading))

head(pc1_loadings, 5)

# PC1 is dominated by claims-utilisation variables:
# num_claims, claim_amount, avg_past_claim, num_hospital_admissions, num_prescriptions
# all load positively and strongly. PC1 is a "utilisation intensity" axis —
# policyholders with high PC1 scores are heavy users of the health system.
# The variable with the largest positive loading is typically num_claims or claim_amount.
```

```{r task5-scoreplot}
pca_scores |>
  bind_cols(health_small |> select(plan_tier)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = plan_tier)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "PCA Score Plot: PC1 vs PC2 by Plan Tier",
       colour = "Plan Tier") +
  theme_minimal()

# Platinum and Gold policyholders tend to cluster toward higher PC2 scores
# (higher premium, higher coverage_amount), while Bronze clusters near the origin.
# On PC1, all tiers overlap substantially — utilisation intensity does not
# cleanly separate plan tiers, suggesting that risk is distributed across all tiers.
```
